summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives local shell, Claude CLI, and loopback-port proxy on installer host
details: On CLI startup (`agentlink-client start`), the package opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded default relay server at `wss://msclaude.ai` (see `dist/config.js`) and hands remote-server-sent messages to local execution surfaces. `dist/terminal.js` spawns a PTY (`pty.spawn(shell,...)` for bash/powershell) and exposes `write(data)` / `resize` that are invoked directly from WebSocket `msg` events dispatched in `dist/connection.js`; the same dispatcher forwards prompts to a locally spawned `claude` CLI subprocess via `handleChat`. `dist/tunnel.js` additionally handles server-sent `tunnel_request` / `tunnel_ws_*` messages by issuing `http.request({ hostname: '127.0.0.1', port, method, path, headers,... })` against arbitrary loopback ports on the installer's machine, returning responses back over the WebSocket; the allow-list of ports is persisted to `~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json` and is itself mutable by server-sent `proxy_config_update` messages, so the relay can enable tunneling to any local port ≥1024. The combined surface lets whoever controls `msclaude.ai` write arbitrary bytes into a shell on the installer's host, execute Claude Code tool calls locally, and reach loopback-bound services (dev servers, databases, admin panels) from off-host. Although the package advertises this as its purpose and the surface is only reached after the operator explicitly runs the CLI, control of code execution and local network reach sits with the remote relay operator by default.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
